ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a circle with center labeled U. Points P, Q, R, S, and T lie on the circle in cyclic order P-Q-R-S-T. The angle PQR is formed at Q by chords QP and QR. Reasoning: Since pentagon PQRST is equilateral and inscribed in the same circle, its five equal sides are equal chords, so the five minor arcs between consecutive vertices are equal. Each arc measures 360/5 = 72 degrees. Angle PQR intercepts the arc from P to R that does not contain Q; from the diagram this arc goes P-T-S-R, consisting of three equal arcs. Thus the intercepted arc measures 3*72 = 216 degrees. By the inscribed angle theorem, m angle PQR = 216/2 = 108 degrees.
